summary: The core is organised as a board netlist: parts are instantiated under PCB location names (u13A 6809, u9A Z80, u11D 005885, u8F/u7F/u9F/u6F EPROMs, u3F-u5F colour PROMs), and the Konami 005885 is a module whose ports are the chip's pins. Inside the 005885, video comes from 9-bit H/V counters, with tile fetches latched on H counter bit edges, a per-line sprite scan into a double line buffer, and a per-pixel tile/sprite mux driving external LUT PROMs. None of it follows MAME's tilemap/draw_sprites/scanline_tick decomposition. The only overlaps with MAME are memory-map and data-format facts that any correct core must share.

findings.signal: Board-level netlist with PCB part designators
findings.note: Every CPU, ROM, PROM, RAM and custom chip is a separate instance named by board location (u13A, u9A, u11D, u8F, u11F, u3F...) and wired net by net, not grouped into MAME-style functional handlers.

findings.signal: 005885 modelled with its own pins as ports
findings.mame_ref: ironhors.cpp: no 005885 device; video lives in driver functions
findings.note: Ports are the chip's pins (NCK2, H1O, NCPE/NCPQ, VCF/VCB/VCD, OCF/OCB/OCD, COL, NXCS, NIOC, NCSY, NFIR/NIRQ/NNMI, R/S ROM buses). The colour lookup is done by external PROMs on the board instead of inside the chip, unlike MAME, which folds the lookup into its palette init.

9-bit h_cnt/v_cnt with reload values (511->128, vcnt_end->vcnt_start), blanking and sync decoded from counter values at the 6.144 MHz pixel enable, instead of a screen configuration with visible-area rectangles.

NMI fires on the falling edge of v_cnt[5] (or v_cnt[4]), IRQ on the VBlank edge, and FIRQ on VBlank gated by an odd/even frame flip-flop. MAME instead tests (scanline+16)%64 and scanline==240 in a timer callback.

findings.signal: Tilemap fetch pipeline latched on H-counter edges
findings.note: VRAM is addressed from scrolled counter bits, and attribute, code and ROM data are latched on the rising/falling edges of h_cnt[2] and h_cnt[1]. Fine scroll is done with a 32-bit pixel shift register and the row scroll comes from ZRAM addressed by vpos. There is no tile_info callback or per-row set_scrollx batch.

findings.signal: External attribute bit latched by board logic
findings.note: VRAM data bit 5 leaves the chip on ATR5 and is clocked through two flops by an H4 divider made from H1O, then fed into tile EPROM address bit 13. MAME just adds the bit into the tile code arithmetically.

findings.signal: Per-line sprite scan into double line buffer
findings.note: On each line a state machine walks the 5-byte sprite entries, tests whether each sprite covers the line by subtracting the vertical position, and writes pixels into a ping-pong line buffer (bank = vpos[0]) that is read out at pixel rate. MAME blits whole gfx elements per frame and splits 16x8/8x16 sprites into two 8x8 draws.

findings.signal: Per-pixel priority mux on sprite transparency
findings.note: A pixel-rate mux selects tile or sprite from the sprite-nonzero bit and drives a 5-bit COL bus, whose top bit selects the sprite/char half of the colour PROMs. MAME draws the tilemap and then sprites with transpen.

I/O selects are built from the chip's NIOC pin plus A[10:8], the way discrete decoders on the board would be, rather than from a map table. The addresses themselves are shared with MAME's master_map, which is expected.

findings.signal: Behaviour MAME lacks: bootleg timing quirks, sprite limit
findings.note: The core models bootleg PCB anomalies, including extra vertical lines, shifted HBlank, a lower sprite limit and a sprite layer offset by one line. These are all expressed as counter-compare changes, which is how hardware would produce them; MAME does not model them.

The sprite byte fields (code bits, colour nibble, size bits, flip bits) decode to the same values as MAME's code/size switch. This is a data format any correct implementation must share, and the decode is spread across FSM states rather than copied from the C.

findings.signal: Switchable SSG filters via YM2203 IOA
findings.note: The filter enables come from the IOA port bits, as in MAME's discrete-sound writes. The filters themselves are generic IIR blocks, which is FPGA engineering and counts for neither side.
